subject: chemistry
title: Equilibrium Adventure 3: Kc, Kp and ΔG at equilibrium
welcome_lead: Today you'll connect Kc to ΔG via the Gibbs equation.
meta_desc: IBDP Chemistry HL — relationship Kc ↔ Kp, ΔG = -RT ln K, feasibility.
final_note: You learned ΔG = -RT ln K; spontaneous when K > 1 (negative ΔG); Kp from partial pressures, Kc from concentrations.

concepts.def: Q < K → forward; Q > K → reverse

walkthroughs.body_html:
For gases, Kp uses partial pressures instead of concentrations.

p(A) × V = n(A)RT, so [A] = p(A)/RT.

Kp = Kc · (RT)^Δn where Δn = (moles gas product) - (moles gas reactant).

ΔG° = -RT ln K

- K = 1 → ΔG° = 0 (equilibrium 50:50).
- K > 1 → ΔG° < 0 → spontaneous as written.
- K < 1 → ΔG° > 0 → non-spontaneous (reverse spontaneous).

At any moment, Q has the same form as K but with current concentrations.

- Q < K → reaction goes forward.
- Q > K → reaction goes reverse.
- Q = K → no net change (at equilibrium).

ΔG = ΔG° + RT ln Q. At Q = K, ΔG = 0.
